newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise as transport shares surge.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise as transport shares surge.

text.p: Stocks rose Friday, led by a surge in transportation shares which finally showed signs of emerging from their summer-long malaise.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 19.61 points to 5,887.35. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 11 to eight on active volume of 332 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow Jones Transportation Index soared 31.68 points, or 1.53 percent, to 2,095.58.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 6.61 points to 1,218.70.

Since the broad market sell-off in early July, several indices, most notably the Dow, have recouped their losses and pushed through to new record levels. However, as a group, the transports have largely failed to participate in the recovery.
"When you get further and further into a rally, you start to look at the laggards," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities. "One of the laggards has been the transport index."
Even as the transportation sector played catch-up, some broader indices hit new highs early Friday in a rally that analysts said seems to be picking up steam.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks gained 3.07 to 686.07 after reaching a record 687.07 in earlier trade. The S&P 100 was up 3.23 to 663.72 after hitting an all-time high of 664.91 earlier.
"The S&P 100 is breaking out to the upside and that is a very bullish sign," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Bleier noted, however, that the S&P 100, like the Dow industrials, is comprised of the very large capitalisation stocks that have become investor favourites of late.
"We have seen some filtering down to small-cap names but this rally continues to be selective," Bleier said.

The heavy trading volume generally would have been viewed as another bullish sign. But analysts attibuted much of the volume to the "triple witching" expiration of options and futures, which inflate volume levels and occasionally produce temporary price fluctuations.

Among individual issues, Hughes Electronics Corp. jumped 3-3/8 to 61-1/8 after the company announced it would acquire satellite concern Panamsat Corp. for $30 per share. Shares in PanAmSat were unchanged at 27-3/4.

Houston Exploration Co., a natural gas exploration unit of Brooklyn Union Gas Co., gained 1-1/2 to 17 on its first day of trading. Shares in Brooklyn Union, which offered 7.1 million shares in the unit, rose 1/4 to 27-1/4.
America Online Inc. rose 2 to 35-1/8. The shares have gained more than 8 since the company's NYSE debut on Monday.
